title: Manual handling for cleaning work
audience: All cleaners and supervisors in any cleaning-group business, including workers who lift, carry, push or pull equipment, bins, consumables and furniture, and workers who reach to clean high or low surfaces.
learningOutcomes: Identify the manual handling tasks in a cleaning job, including carrying, pushing, pulling, lifting and reaching.
Assess a load or a movement before it is attempted, and decide whether to reduce it, split it, use an aid, or get help.
Apply the controls for manual handling: planned routes, mechanical aids, team lifts and working within reach.
Report a manual handling hazard, strain or near miss, and name the control that was used.

instruction.heading: Status of this lesson
instruction.body: The uploaded source gives the title of a manual handling annex but not its text. The only manual handling statement in the source is a short line about keeping to manageable areas, and it is used here. The rest of this lesson is a general outline written by the team. This lesson grants no licence or certificate.

instruction.heading: Where manual handling happens
instruction.body: Manual handling is any task that involves lifting, lowering, pushing, pulling, carrying, holding or reaching. In cleaning work it appears when you move a full bucket, a vacuum, a floor machine, a bin of waste, a box of stock, a ladder or a piece of furniture, and when you stretch to reach a high or low surface. Repetition matters as much as weight. Many small movements repeated through a shift can cause as much harm as one heavy lift.

instruction.heading: Plan the movement before you start
instruction.body: Before you lift or move anything, look at the load, the route you will take, and the place where it will be set down. Check any weight that is marked on the container. Clear the route of trip hazards and wet patches. If the load is unstable, awkward, too heavy for one person, or blocks your view, do not attempt it alone.

instruction.heading: Use aids and a second person
instruction.body: Use a trolley or a cart, a hoist where the site provides one, or a second person for a load that is large or heavy. Where a load can be divided, divide it rather than making one difficult trip. When you lift with someone else, agree a signal beforehand so that you both lift and set down at the same moment.

instruction.heading: Keep the body in a safe position
instruction.body: Keep the load close to your body, keep your back in its natural position, and move with your legs rather than twisting your trunk. Avoid bending and twisting at the same time, and avoid reaching far above the shoulders or far out in front of the body. Where the work allows it, change position and take short breaks between tasks.

instruction.heading: Work in manageable areas
instruction.body: Clean in areas that you can reach and control comfortably. Move the equipment rather than leaning, stretching or overbalancing to reach a surface. The stairs procedure in “Cleaning stairs, landings, balustrades and handrails” uses the same principle, which is to work in a manageable area rather than attempting a whole stairwell in one movement.

instruction.heading: Reporting and records
instruction.body: Report any sore back, strain, near miss or unsafe load to your supervisor on the same day. Record the task, the load or the movement, the control that was used, and whether help was needed. Repeated reports about the same task are a signal that the task or the equipment needs to change.

instruction.heading: Legal position
instruction.body: They must be checked before this policy is finalised.

procedure: Identify each manual handling task in the job, including the movement of equipment, waste and consumables.
Look at the load, any weight marking, the route and the place where the load will be set down.
Decide whether you can manage the load on your own. If you cannot, get a trolley or a second person, or divide the load.
Clear the route of trip hazards, wet floors and obstacles before you move.
Stand close to the load with your feet apart, and keep your back in its natural position.
Lift with your legs, keeping the load close to your body. Do not twist while you lift.
When lifting with someone else, use the agreed signal and move at the same time.
Set the load down with the same care, and do not drop it.
Work in areas that are within easy reach. Move the equipment rather than stretching or leaning.
Report any strain, sore area, near miss or unsafe load the same day, and record the control that was used.

workedExamples.situation: You need to take a full bucket of water up a flight of stairs.
workedExamples.reasoning: Do not carry a heavy bucket up the stairs in one hand. Divide the water into smaller containers, or use a trolley where the site has one, and carry the load close to your body. When the steps are wet, dry the route first or wait until they are safe. Stop and get help if the load is too heavy to hold steady.

workedExamples.situation: A box of chemical containers is on a high shelf above a washroom, and you have to stretch to reach it.
workedExamples.reasoning: Do not stretch, and do not stand on a bin or a chair. Use a step ladder only if the business has authorised it and you have been trained to use it. Otherwise call your supervisor. Leave the box where it is until a safe method is available. The stop-work rule for height in “Window cleaning from the ground and with extension equipment” applies to any reach that needs a ladder or platform.

workedExamples.situation: You push a heavy floor machine across a carpet and feel a pull in your lower back.
workedExamples.reasoning: Stop using the machine, take the weight off your back, and tell your supervisor the same day. Record the task, the machine, the surface and the control that was used. The supervisor then checks whether a second person, a different machine or a changed route is needed.

equipmentAndPpe: A trolley or cart for heavy or bulky loads.
Gloves and footwear with good grip.
Weight and handling markings on containers and boxes.
A step ladder or stool, only where the business has authorised it and the worker is trained to use it.
An agreed lifting signal for any task that needs two people.

commonErrors.error: Carrying a heavy load up stairs in one hand to save a trip.
commonErrors.prevention: Divide the load, use a trolley, or get help before you lift.

commonErrors.error: Twisting the trunk while lifting or while setting a load down.
commonErrors.prevention: Turn your feet rather than your trunk, and keep the load close to your body.

commonErrors.error: Stretching or standing on an unstable item to reach a high surface.
commonErrors.prevention: Move the equipment closer, or stop and call your supervisor.

commonErrors.error: Lifting with a partner without agreeing when to lift.
commonErrors.prevention: Agree a signal and move together.

commonErrors.error: Ignoring a sore back and carrying on with the same task.
commonErrors.prevention: Report the discomfort the same day so the task can be reviewed.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Do not lift, carry or push a load that you cannot control. Get help, a trolley, or divide the load.

Check the manual handling duties in work health and safety law, the code of practice that applies, and any load limit in each state and territory with the relevant regulator before relying on this point.
Reaching to a shelf or a surface that needs a ladder, platform or step is outside this lesson. Stop and report.
Trip hazards on the route, such as wet floors, cables and equipment left in walkways, must be cleared or marked before a load is moved.

qualityStandard: Each manual handling task is identified before the work starts.
Loads that are too heavy or awkward are divided, moved with an aid, or moved by two people.
No twisting while lifting, and no stretching onto an unstable item.
Every strain, near miss or unsafe load is reported on the same day.
documentationEvidence: Task note for each task that involves a lift, a carry or a repeated reach, reviewed by the supervisor.
Incident or near-miss record for any strain or near miss, showing the control that was used.
Record of any trolley, aid or second person used for a task.
Supervisor review note where the same task has been reported more than once.
summary: Plan each movement: check the load, the route and the place it will be set down.
Use a trolley, divide the load, or get a second person before you lift something heavy or awkward.
Lift with your legs and keep the load close. Do not twist while lifting.
Report any strain or near miss on the same day, and record the control that was used.

knowledgeChecks.question: Which of these is a manual handling task in cleaning work?
options: Reading a safety data sheet at a desk and then taking a short break
Carrying a full waste bin along a corridor to the bin store
Filling in the cleaning checklist and then signing it at the desk

knowledgeChecks.question: A load is too heavy and awkward to lift alone. What is the correct first action?
options: Lift it quickly with a twist so the job is done in one go
Stretch onto a chair so the load clears the floor, then lift from there
Divide the load, use a trolley, or get a second person before you lift

knowledgeChecks.question: A cleaner feels a pull in the lower back after pushing a heavy machine. What is the correct response?
options: Stop, take the load off your back, and report it to your supervisor the same day
Keep working and see whether it eases before the shift finishes and it may pass by itself
Ask a colleague to finish the task and say nothing about it to the supervisor
